questions.title: Select all students
questions.description: Write a query to return every column from the students table.
hints: Use SELECT * from students
questions.explanation: The asterisk selects all columns from the specified table.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students

questions.title: Select specific student columns
questions.description: Return only first name, last name, and email of all students.
hints: List the column names you need
Separate them with commas
questions.explanation: Selecting specific columns is more efficient than SELECT * when you only need certain fields.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, email FROM students

questions.title: Select distinct departments
questions.description: Show all unique department IDs from the students table.
hints: Use DISTINCT to eliminate duplicates
Target the department_id column
questions.explanation: DISTINCT removes duplicate values from the result set.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT DISTINCT department_id FROM students

questions.title: Select active students full name
questions.description: Return the first name and last name of students who are Active.
hints: Add a WHERE clause to filter by status
Remember status values include Active
questions.explanation: Filtering with WHERE lets you narrow down results to records meeting a condition.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE status = 'Active'

questions.title: Count all students
questions.description: How many students are in the database? Return the count.
hints: Use COUNT(*) to count all rows
No WHERE clause needed — count everything
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) returns the total number of rows in a table.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_students FROM students

questions.title: Select students with GPA above 3.5
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, and gpa for students with GPA greater than 3.5.
hints: Filter with WHERE gpa > 3.5
questions.explanation: Comparison operators like > work directly on numeric columns.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa > 3.5

questions.title: Select students enrolled in 2022
questions.description: Return first_name and enrollment_date for students who enrolled in 2022.
hints: Filter by enrollment_date between Jan 1 2022 and Dec 31 2022
Use >= and < for date ranges
questions.explanation: Date comparisons in SQLite work lexicographically with YYYY-MM-DD format.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, enrollment_date FROM students WHERE enrollment_date >= '2022-01-01' AND enrollment_date < '2023-01-01'

questions.title: Select teachers in CS department
questions.description: Return first name and last name of teachers whose department_id is 1.
hints: Filter teachers by department_id = 1
questions.explanation: Simple equality filter retrieves all matching rows.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM teachers WHERE department_id = 1

questions.title: Select books under 12 dollars
questions.description: Return title and price of books costing less than $12.
hints: Filter with WHERE price < 12
questions.explanation: Relational operators can filter any numeric column.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT title, price FROM books WHERE price < 12.00

questions.title: Select students not in department 1
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name for students NOT in Computer Science (department_id != 1).
hints: Use <> or != for NOT EQUAL
questions.explanation: The <> operator checks for inequality.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE department_id <> 1

questions.title: Select students with NULL advisor
questions.description: Return first_name and last_name of students whose advisor_teacher_id is NULL.
hints: Use IS NULL to check for null values
NOT = NULL does NOT work in SQL
questions.explanation: SQL uses IS NULL / IS NOT NULL instead of = / != for null checks.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE advisor_teacher_id IS NULL

questions.title: Select female students
questions.description: Return first_name and gender of all female students.
hints: Filter by gender = Female
Select two columns
questions.explanation: String literals in SQL are wrapped in single quotes.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, gender FROM students WHERE gender = 'Female'

questions.title: Select active students in Illinois
questions.description: Return first_name, city, state for active students in Illinois.
hints: Combine conditions with AND
Match both status and state
questions.explanation: AND combines multiple conditions — all must be true.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, city, state FROM students WHERE status = 'Active' AND state = 'IL'

questions.title: Select teachers hired after 2015
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, hire_date for teachers hired after January 1, 2015.
hints: Filter by hire_date > '2015-01-01'
Include hire_date in output
questions.explanation: Date strings in ISO format sort correctly with comparison operators.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, hire_date FROM teachers WHERE hire_date > '2015-01-01'

questions.title: Select courses subject 2 Fall 2023
questions.description: Return course_number, section, room for courses in subject 2, semester Fall, year 2023.
hints: Chain three conditions with AND
Match subject_id, semester, and year
questions.explanation: Multiple AND conditions narrow results incrementally.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT course_number, section, room FROM courses WHERE subject_id = 2 AND semester = 'Fall' AND year = 2023

questions.title: Students with GPA between 3.0 and 3.5
questions.description: Return first_name and gpa for students whose GPA is between 3.0 and 3.5 inclusive.
hints: BETWEEN is inclusive on both ends
Use BETWEEN low AND high
questions.explanation: BETWEEN simplifies range queries — it includes both boundary values.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa BETWEEN 3.0 AND 3.5

questions.title: Teachers in specific departments
questions.description: Return first_name and department_id for teachers in departments 1, 2, or 3.
hints: Use IN to check against a list of values
List the department ids
questions.explanation: IN(...) is shorthand for multiple OR conditions.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, department_id FROM teachers WHERE department_id IN (1, 2, 3)

questions.title: Last name starts with J
questions.description: Return first_name and last_name of students whose last name begins with the letter J.
hints: Use LIKE with wildcard %
Last name starting with J means J%
questions.explanation: The % wildcard matches zero or more characters.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE last_name LIKE 'J%'

questions.title: Students with phone numbers
questions.description: Return first_name and phone for students who have a non-null phone number.
hints: Filter where phone IS NOT NULL
These students provided contact info
questions.explanation: IS NOT NULL finds records with actual values in a column.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, phone FROM students WHERE phone IS NOT NULL

questions.title: Books published 1940 to 1965
questions.description: Return title and published_year for books published between 1940 and 1965 inclusive.
hints: Use BETWEEN for the year range
Include both endpoints
questions.explanation: Years stored as integers support direct BETWEEN comparison.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT title, published_year FROM books WHERE published_year BETWEEN 1940 AND 1965

questions.title: Active loans due after Jan 2024
questions.description: Return student_id, book_id, due_date for active loans with due dates after 2024-01-31.
hints: Filter by status = Active
Also filter by due_date > 2024-01-31
Combine with AND
questions.explanation: Combining text status with date filters requires AND.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT student_id, book_id, due_date FROM loans WHERE status = 'Active' AND due_date > '2024-01-31'

questions.title: Courses with specific subjects
questions.description: Return course_number and subject_id for courses in subjects 1, 2, 3, or 5.
hints: Filter with IN clause
Match specific subject IDs
questions.explanation: IN works with integer lists too, not just strings.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT course_number, subject_id FROM courses WHERE subject_id IN (1, 2, 3, 5)

questions.title: Enrollments with grades
questions.description: Return student_id and grade for enrollments where grade indicates completion (not NULL).
hints: Filter where grade IS NOT NULL
These represent completed enrollments
questions.explanation: Grades may be NULL for currently in-progress courses.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT student_id, grade FROM enrollments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL

questions.title: Authors born before 1900
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, birth_year for authors born before 1900.
hints: Use < to find earlier birth years
questions.explanation: Less-than comparisons on integers are straightforward.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, birth_year FROM authors WHERE birth_year < 1900

questions.title: Departments budget over 200k
questions.description: Return name and budget for departments with budget exceeding 200,000.
hints: Filter by budget > 200000
Only some departments exceed this threshold
questions.explanation: Budget filtering helps identify well-funded departments.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT name, budget FROM departments WHERE budget > 200000

questions.title: Students ordered by GPA descending
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, gpa ordered by GPA from highest to lowest.
hints: Use ORDER BY gpa DESC
DESC means descending (highest first)
questions.explanation: ORDER BY arranges results; DESC puts largest values first.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, gpa FROM students ORDER BY gpa DESC

questions.title: Teachers ordered by salary ascending
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, salary ordered by salary from lowest to highest.
hints: Use ORDER BY salary ASC
ASC is default but explicit is clearer
questions.explanation: ASCENDING order shows smallest values first.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary FROM teachers ORDER BY salary ASC

questions.title: Top 5 students by GPA
questions.description: Return the top 5 students by GPA (first_name, last_name, gpa).
hints: Order by gpa DESC first
Then add LIMIT 5 to take the top 5
questions.explanation: LIMIT restricts the number of returned rows.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, gpa FROM students ORDER BY gpa DESC LIMIT 5

questions.title: Students enrolled in 2021 ordered by name
questions.description: Return first_name, enrollment_date for students enrolled in 2021, ordered by first_name.
hints: Filter for enrollment_date in 2021
Order by first_name ASC
Year range uses >= start and < next year
questions.explanation: Range filters combined with ORDER BY give organized results.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, enrollment_date FROM students WHERE enrollment_date >= '2021-01-01' AND enrollment_date < '2022-01-01' ORDER BY first_name

questions.title: Expensive books
questions.description: Return title and price of books ordered by price from most expensive to least.
hints: ORDER BY price DESC
No additional filtering needed
questions.explanation: ORDER BY without WHERE returns all rows sorted.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT title, price FROM books ORDER BY price DESC

questions.title: Last 3 students by enrollment date
questions.description: Return first_name, enrollment_date of the 3 most recently enrolled students.
hints: ORDER BY enrollment_date DESC to get latest first
Then LIMIT 3
Most recent enrollments come last alphabetically in date format
questions.explanation: Descending date order brings newest entries to the top.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, enrollment_date FROM students ORDER BY enrollment_date DESC LIMIT 3

questions.title: Departments by budget
questions.description: Return name and budget of departments ordered by budget descending.
hints: ORDER BY budget DESC
Return name and budget columns
questions.explanation: Budget is a REAL type; DESC shows highest budgets first.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT name, budget FROM departments ORDER BY budget DESC

questions.title: Students by GPA then last name
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, gpa ordered by GPA descending, then last_name ascending as tiebreaker.
hints: Primary sort by gpa DESC
Secondary sort by last_name ASC for ties
Multiple ORDER BY columns create tiebreakers
questions.explanation: When GPA values match, the secondary sort orders those rows.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, gpa FROM students ORDER BY gpa DESC, last_name ASC

questions.title: Total number of students
questions.description: How many students are registered?
hints: COUNT(*) counts all rows
Alias the result as total_students
questions.explanation: Aggregate functions operate on entire columns.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_students FROM students

questions.title: Average GPA of all students
questions.description: Calculate the average GPA across all students.
hints: Use AVG(gpa) to compute mean
AVG ignores NULL values
questions.explanation: AVG() returns the arithmetic mean of non-null values.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT AVG(gpa) AS avg_gpa FROM students

questions.title: Maximum and minimum salaries
questions.description: Find the highest and lowest teacher salaries.
hints: MAX(salary) for highest
MIN(salary) for lowest
Use both aggregates in one query
questions.explanation: Multiple aggregates can run simultaneously in one SELECT.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS max_salary, MIN(salary) AS min_salary FROM teachers

questions.title: Total book inventory value
questions.description: Calculate the total value of all books (sum of price * stock).
hints: Multiply price by stock per row
Then SUM the results
SQLite supports expressions inside aggregates
questions.explanation: Arithmetic inside aggregates lets you compute derived totals.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT SUM(price * stock) AS total_value FROM books

questions.title: Count of active teachers
questions.description: How many teachers are currently active?
hints: Filter is_active = 1
Then COUNT(*)
Only active teachers count
questions.explanation: Combining COUNT with WHERE restricts the aggregation scope.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS active_teachers FROM teachers WHERE is_active = 1

questions.title: Total scholarship money awarded
questions.description: What is the total amount of scholarships awarded to students?
hints: SUM(amount_awarded) from student_scholarships
One simple aggregate over the junction table
questions.explanation: The junction table tracks individual awards with amounts.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT SUM(amount_awarded) AS total_scholarship FROM student_scholarships

questions.title: Department budget summary
questions.description: Return department name, count of teachers, and total salary budget per department.
hints: LEFT JOIN departments with teachers
COUNT and SUM the teacher data
GROUP BY department
Order by total salary descending
Departments with no teachers still appear thanks to LEFT JOIN
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN ensures departments with zero teachers still show up.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(t.id) AS teacher_count, SUM(t.salary) AS total_salary FROM departments d LEFT JOIN teachers t ON d.id = t.department_id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ORDER BY total_salary DESC

questions.title: Average exam score per course
questions.description: For each course, show the average marks obtained across all exam results.
hints: Join exams with exam_results
AVG(marks_obtained) grouped by course_id
ROUND to 1 decimal place
GROUP BY groups results by course
questions.explanation: JOINs enable aggregations across related tables.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT e.course_id, ROUND(AVG(er.marks_obtained), 1) AS avg_marks FROM exams e JOIN exam_results er ON e.id = er.exam_id GROUP BY e.course_id

questions.title: Student count per department
questions.description: Count how many students are in each department.
hints: GROUP BY department_id
COUNT(*) for each group
Order doesn't matter unless requested
questions.explanation: GROUP BY collapses rows sharing the same value into one aggregate row.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS student_count FROM students GROUP BY department_id

questions.title: Average GPA per department
questions.description: Calculate the average GPA for each department.
hints: GROUP BY department_id
AVG(gpa) for each group
ROUND to 2 decimal places
questions.explanation: ROUND(x, 2) trims floating point precision for readability.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT department_id, ROUND(AVG(gpa), 2) AS avg_gpa FROM students GROUP BY department_id

questions.title: Courses per subject
questions.description: How many course sections exist for each subject?
hints: GROUP BY subject_id
COUNT(*) measures sections per subject
questions.explanation: A subject can have multiple course sections (different semesters/teachers).
questions.solutionSql: SELECT subject_id, COUNT(*) AS course_count FROM courses GROUP BY subject_id

questions.title: Departments with more than 3 students
questions.description: Return department_id and student count, but only for departments with more than 3 students.
hints: GROUP BY department_id
HAVING filters groups (not individual rows)
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3 keeps only crowded departments
questions.explanation: HAVING applies after grouping; WHERE applies before grouping.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS student_count FROM students GROUP BY department_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3

questions.title: Enrollment status distribution
questions.description: Count enrollments by their status (Enrolled, Completed, In Progress, etc.).
hints: GROUP BY status
COUNT(*) per status
ORDER BY count DESC for readability
questions.explanation: Status values partition enrollments into categories.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM enrollments GROUP BY status ORDER BY enrollment_count DESC

questions.title: Book categories with total stock
questions.description: Return category and total stock count per book category.
hints: GROUP BY category
SUM(stock) totals inventory per category
ORDER BY total_stock DESC
questions.explanation: Categories group books by genre/type; stock sums inventory.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT category, SUM(stock) AS total_stock FROM books GROUP BY category ORDER BY total_stock DESC

questions.title: Students with multiple enrollments
questions.description: Find student IDs who are enrolled in more than one course (completed or in progress).
hints: Filter to relevant statuses first
GROUP BY student_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
Only students taking multiple courses
questions.explanation: Multi-table or filtered GROUP BY narrows to active participants.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS course_count FROM enrollments WHERE status IN ('Completed', 'In Progress') GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

questions.title: Average attendance by course
questions.description: For completed enrollments, find the average attendance percentage per course.
hints: WHERE status = Completed first
AVG(attendance_percentage) per course
HAVING avg >= 80 filters low-attendance courses
ROUND to 1 decimal place
ORDER BY avg_attendance DESC
questions.explanation: Complex GROUP BY chains require careful filter ordering.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT course_id, ROUND(AVG(attendance_percentage), 1) AS avg_attendance FROM enrollments WHERE status = 'Completed' GROUP BY course_id HAVING AVG(attendance_percentage) >= 80 ORDER BY avg_attendance DESC

questions.title: Student and department names
questions.description: Return student first_name, last_name, and their department name.
hints: JOIN students with departments
ON department_id matches id
Alias departments.name as department_name
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN returns only rows with matches in both tables.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, d.name AS department_name FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.department_id = d.id

questions.title: Teacher and department
questions.description: Return teacher first_name, last_name, and department name.
hints: JOIN teachers to departments
ON department_id = departments.id
questions.explanation: Self-explanatory: link teacher records to department names.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT t.first_name, t.last_name, d.name AS department FROM teachers t JOIN departments d ON t.department_id = d.id

questions.title: Course with subject and teacher
questions.description: Return course_number, subject name, and teacher full name for all courses.
hints: JOIN courses to subjects on subject_id
JOIN courses to teachers on teacher_id
Concatenate teacher names with ||
questions.explanation: Multiple JOINs chain relationships across three tables.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT c.course_number, sub.name AS subject_name, t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS teacher_name FROM courses c JOIN subjects sub ON c.subject_id = sub.id JOIN teachers t ON c.teacher_id = t.id

questions.title: Enrollment details with student and course
questions.description: Return student first_name, last_name, course_number, and grade for all enrollments.
hints: JOIN enrollments to students on student_id
JOIN enrollments to courses on course_id
Select name + course_number + grade
questions.explanation: Enrollments is the bridge table connecting students and courses.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, c.course_number, e.grade FROM enrollments e JOIN students s ON e.student_id = s.id JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id

questions.title: Books with their authors
questions.description: Return book title and author full name for all books.
hints: JOIN books to book_authors on book_id
JOIN book_authors to authors on author_id
Concatenate author first and last name
Many-to-many relationship via book_authors
questions.explanation: book_authors is the junction table resolving the many-to-many between books and authors.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT b.title, a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS author_name FROM books b JOIN book_authors ba ON b.id = ba.book_id JOIN authors a ON ba.author_id = a.id

questions.title: Students with their exams and scores
questions.description: Return student first_name, last_name, exam title, and marks obtained for all exam results.
hints: JOIN exam_results to students on student_id
JOIN exam_results to exams on exam_id
Three-way join
Select names, exam title, and marks
questions.explanation: Exam results sit between students and exams as the associative table.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, e.title, er.marks_obtained FROM exam_results er JOIN students s ON er.student_id = s.id JOIN exams e ON er.exam_id = e.id

questions.title: Loans with student and book details
questions.description: Return student first_name, last_name, book title, loan_date, and status for all loans.
hints: JOIN loans to students on student_id
JOIN loans to books on book_id
Two JOINs from loans (junction table)
questions.explanation: Loans links students and books together via foreign keys.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, b.title, l.loan_date, l.status FROM loans l JOIN students s ON l.student_id = s.id JOIN books b ON l.book_id = b.id

questions.title: Courses with enrolled student count
questions.description: Return course_number, section, and the count of currently enrolled/in-progress students.
hints: LEFT JOIN courses with enrollments
Filter enrollment status in JOIN condition
COUNT(e.id) counts only matched enrollments
GROUP BY course fields
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN ensures courses with zero current students still appear.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT c.course_number, c.section, COUNT(e.id) AS enrolled_students FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON c.id = e.course_id AND e.status IN ('Enrolled', 'In Progress') GROUP BY c.id, c.course_number, c.section

questions.title: Department head teachers
questions.description: Return department name and the head teacher's full name.
hints: LEFT JOIN departments to teachers on head_teacher_id
Some departments may have no head (NULL head_teacher_id)
Use LEFT JOIN to preserve all departments
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN is essential when the foreign key might be NULL.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT d.name AS department_name, t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS head_teacher FROM departments d LEFT JOIN teachers t ON d.head_teacher_id = t.id

questions.title: Students with failing grades
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, course_number, grade for enrollments where grade indicates failure.
hints: JOIN enrollments to students to courses
Filter for failing grade values
Use IN for the grade list
questions.explanation: Grade letters follow a standard academic scale.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, c.course_number, e.grade FROM enrollments e JOIN students s ON e.student_id = s.id JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id WHERE e.grade IN ('F', 'D+', 'D', 'D-', 'F+')

questions.title: Scholarship recipients with student details
questions.description: Return student first_name, last_name, scholarship name, and amount awarded.
hints: JOIN student_scholarships to students
JOIN student_scholarships to scholarships
Select names, scholarship name, and amount
ORDER BY amount DESC
questions.explanation: student_scholarships bridges students and scholarships in a many-to-many.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, sh.name AS scholarship_name, ss.amount_awarded FROM student_scholarships ss JOIN students s ON ss.student_id = s.id JOIN scholarships sh ON ss.scholarship_id = sh.id ORDER BY ss.amount_awarded DESC

questions.title: Exam performance per student per course
questions.description: Return student first_name, last_name, course_number, exam title, marks_obtained, total_marks.
hints: Four-table JOIN: exam_results to students to exams to courses
Select name, course, exam title, marks, total
ORDER BY last name then exam date
Shows full performance picture
questions.explanation: Chain four tables to get the complete exam performance record.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, c.course_number, e.title, er.marks_obtained, e.total_marks FROM exam_results er JOIN students s ON er.student_id = s.id JOIN exams e ON er.exam_id = e.id JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id ORDER BY s.last_name, e.exam_date

questions.title: Students above average GPA
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, gpa for students whose GPA is above the average GPA of all students.
hints: Subquery in WHERE: find AVG(gpa) first
Outer query filters students above that average
Parentheses around subquery are required
questions.explanation: A scalar subquery returns one value used in the outer WHERE clause.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa > (SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students)

questions.title: Courses taught by CS teachers
questions.description: Return course_number for courses taught by a teacher in the Computer Science department (dept id = 1).
hints: Subquery finds CS teacher IDs
Outer query filters courses by those teacher IDs
Use IN for the subquery result
questions.explanation: The subquery runs first, returning IDs used by the outer query.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT course_number FROM courses WHERE teacher_id IN (SELECT id FROM teachers WHERE department_id = 1)

questions.title: Students in same department as Alice Johnson
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name for students in the same department as Alice Johnson (excluding Alice).
hints: Subquery finds Alice's department_id
Outer query finds others in that department
Exclude Alice with != Alice
questions.explanation: Finding a value via subquery then using it in the outer filter is a common pattern.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE department_id = (SELECT department_id FROM students WHERE first_name = 'Alice' AND last_name = 'Johnson') AND first_name != 'Alice'

questions.title: Books in subjects with more than 2 books
questions.description: Return book titles for subjects that have more than 2 books.
hints: Subquery finds subject_ids with > 2 books
Outer query filters books by those subject_ids
GROUP BY + HAVING in subquery
questions.explanation: A grouped subquery can identify qualifying groups first.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT title FROM books WHERE subject_id IN (SELECT subject_id FROM books GROUP BY subject_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2)

questions.title: Students with no enrollments
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name of students who have never been enrolled in any course.
hints: NOT IN subquery finds students absent from enrollments
DISTINCT ensures no duplicates
Students with no enrollments won't appear in the subquery
questions.explanation: NOT IN with a subquery identifies missing relationships.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT student_id FROM enrollments)

questions.title: Courses with enrollment above average
questions.description: Return course_number for courses whose enrollment count exceeds the average enrollment across all courses.
hints: Subquery computes average enrollment
Outer query compares each course's enrolled_count
Use > not >= for strict above-average
questions.explanation: Average enrollment is computed once and reused in every row comparison.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT course_number FROM courses WHERE enrolled_count > (SELECT AVG(enrolled_count) FROM courses)

questions.title: Teachers who have never taught a course
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name of teachers not found in the courses table.
hints: Subquery collects all teacher_ids from courses
NOT IN finds teachers absent from that set
Includes inactive teachers too
questions.explanation: Not-in patterns reveal orphaned or unused entities.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM teachers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT teacher_id FROM courses)

questions.title: Highest scoring exam per course
questions.description: For each course, return the course_number and the highest marks_obtained among its exam results.
hints: JOIN courses to exams to exam_results
MAX(marks_obtained) per course
GROUP BY course
questions.explanation: Aggregating max marks within each course requires joining three tables.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT c.course_number, MAX(er.marks_obtained) AS highest_marks FROM courses c JOIN exams e ON c.id = e.course_id JOIN exam_results er ON e.id = er.exam_id GROUP BY c.id, c.course_number

questions.title: Students who scored above 90
questions.description: Return distinct first_name, last_name of students who got above 90 on at least one exam.
hints: JOIN students to exam_results
Filter marks_obtained > 90
DISTINCT prevents duplicate names
questions.explanation: A student may have multiple high scores; DISTINCT deduplicates.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT DISTINCT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN exam_results er ON s.id = er.student_id WHERE er.marks_obtained > 90

questions.title: Subjects with average exam scores above 80
questions.description: Return subject code and name for subjects whose exam average marks exceed 80.
hints: Nested subquery: group exams by subject
HAVING AVG > 80 finds strong subjects
Outer query gets subject codes and names
questions.explanation: Complex nested subqueries can chain aggregations across multiple levels.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT sub.code, sub.name FROM subjects sub WHERE sub.id IN (SELECT e.subject_id FROM exams e JOIN exam_results er ON e.id = er.exam_id GROUP BY e.subject_id HAVING AVG(er.marks_obtained) > 80)

questions.title: Students and teachers in same city
questions.description: Return first_name and city from students and teachers who share the same city (use UNION).
hints: UNION combines distinct results from two queries
First query gets students
Second gets teachers
UNION removes duplicates automatically
questions.explanation: UNION merges two result sets while eliminating duplicates.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, city FROM students UNION SELECT first_name, city FROM teachers

questions.title: Names from Springfield
questions.description: Return all first_names from students and teachers located in Springfield (no duplicates).
hints: Filter both tables to Springfield
UNION combines distinct names
Both source tables share the same city
questions.explanation: Springfield appears as the city for all sample records.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name FROM students WHERE city = 'Springfield' UNION SELECT first_name FROM teachers WHERE city = 'Springfield'

questions.title: Students NOT in CS department
questions.description: Use EXCEPT to find students not in the Computer Science department (dept_id != 1).
hints: EXCEPT removes matching rows from the first query
First query gets all students
Second gets CS students
Result: non-CS students
questions.explanation: EXCEPT(a, b) returns rows in a but not in b.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name FROM students EXCEPT SELECT first_name FROM students WHERE department_id = 1

questions.title: Courses offered both semesters
questions.description: Use INTERSECT to find course_numbers offered in both Fall 2023 and Spring 2024.
hints: INTERSECT finds common values
First query: Fall 2023 courses
Second: Spring 2024 courses
Intersection = courses offered both semesters
questions.explanation: INTERSECT returns only rows present in BOTH queries.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT course_number FROM courses WHERE semester = 'Fall' AND year = 2023 INTERSECT SELECT course_number FROM courses WHERE semester = 'Spring' AND year = 2024

questions.title: Active students not graduated
questions.description: Use EXCEPT to find students who are Active but not Graduated.
hints: EXCEPT removes graduated names from active list
More robust than WHERE status = Active alone
questions.explanation: EXCEPT handles edge cases better than simple filtering when sets overlap.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name FROM students WHERE status = 'Active' EXCEPT SELECT first_name FROM students WHERE status = 'Graduated'

questions.title: CS department people names
questions.description: Return first_name of people (teachers and students) in Computer Science (dept_id=1), removing duplicates.
hints: Filter teachers to dept_id = 1
Filter students to dept_id = 1
UNION combines without duplicates
questions.explanation: UNION automatically handles duplicate first_name values.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name FROM teachers WHERE department_id = 1 UNION SELECT first_name FROM students WHERE department_id = 1

questions.title: Students who took CS101 and Calculus
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name of students enrolled in both CS101 and MATH101.
hints: Self-join via enrollments twice
Match course_number = CS101 and MATH101
Requires same student in both enrollments
questions.explanation: Cross-referencing the same student across two enrollment records finds shared courses.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e1 ON s.id = e1.student_id JOIN courses c1 ON e1.course_id = c1.id JOIN enrollments e2 ON s.id = e2.student_id JOIN courses c2 ON e2.course_id = c2.id WHERE c1.course_number = 'CS101' AND c2.course_number = 'MATH101'

questions.title: Students with A and F grades
questions.description: Return distinct first_name, last_name of students who have both an A grade and an F grade in any enrollments.
hints: Join enrollments twice on the same student
One copy requires grade = A
Other copy requires grade = F
DISTINCT avoids duplicates
questions.explanation: A student appearing in two enrollment copies with different grades satisfies the condition.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT DISTINCT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e1 ON s.id = e1.student_id JOIN enrollments e2 ON s.id = e2.student_id WHERE e1.grade = 'A' AND e2.grade = 'F'

questions.title: Student full name concatenation
questions.description: Return first_name and last_name concatenated as full_name (space separated).
hints: Use || to concatenate strings
Add a space literal between first and last
Alias as full_name
questions.explanation: SQLite uses || for string concatenation, unlike some databases.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name AS full_name FROM students

questions.title: UPPERCASE student emails
questions.description: Return first_name and their email converted to uppercase.
hints: UPPER() converts a string to uppercase
Apply to the email column
Keep first_name as-is
questions.explanation: UPPER() is a built-in string function in SQLite.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, UPPER(email) AS email_upper FROM students

questions.title: First name length
questions.description: Return first_name and the length of the first name in characters.
hints: LENGTH() counts characters in a string
Select first_name alongside the length
questions.explanation: LENGTH() returns the character count of any text expression.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, LENGTH(first_name) AS name_length FROM students

questions.title: Email containing alice case-insensitive
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name of students whose email contains the substring alice (case-insensitive).
hints: Convert email to lowercase with LOWER()
Use LIKE %alice% for substring match
Case-insensitive because both sides are lowercased
questions.explanation: Converting both sides to the same case enables case-insensitive search.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE LOWER(email) LIKE '%alice%'

questions.title: Extract domain from email
questions.description: Return first_name and the domain part (after @) of the email.
hints: INSTR(email, @) finds position of @
SUBSTR from position+1 extracts the domain
SUBSTR(text, start) gets everything from start onward
questions.explanation: INSTR finds a substring's position; SUBSTR extracts from that point.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1) AS domain FROM students

questions.title: Book titles sorted by first word
questions.description: Return title of books, stripping leading articles (A, An, The) and sorting by the remaining title.
hints: Use CASE to strip leading articles
SUBSTR extracts from the appropriate position
ORDER BY the cleaned title
questions.explanation: String manipulation with CASE enables custom sorting logic.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT title, CASE WHEN LOWER(title) LIKE 'a %' THEN SUBSTR(title, 3) WHEN LOWER(title) LIKE 'an %' THEN SUBSTR(title, 4) WHEN LOWER(title) LIKE 'the %' THEN SUBSTR(title, 5) ELSE title END AS sort_title FROM books ORDER BY sort_title

questions.title: Current date
questions.description: Return the current date.
hints: SQLite has a built-in date(now) function
questions.explanation: date('now') returns today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT date('now')

questions.title: Students age in years
questions.description: Return first_name, date_of_birth, and calculated age in years (as of 2024-01-01).
hints: julianday() converts a date to a Julian day number
Subtract DOB from 2024-01-01
Divide by 365.25 for years
CAST to INTEGER truncates decimals
questions.explanation: julianday enables date arithmetic in SQLite.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, date_of_birth, CAST((julianday('2024-01-01') - julianday(date_of_birth)) / 365.25 AS INTEGER) AS age FROM students

questions.title: Loans overdue as of Feb 2024
questions.description: Return student_id, book_id, due_date for active loans past due as of Feb 1, 2024.
hints: Filter status = Active AND due_date < target date
Any active loan before that date is overdue
questions.explanation: Simple date comparison identifies overdue items.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT student_id, book_id, due_date FROM loans WHERE status = 'Active' AND due_date < '2024-02-01'

questions.title: Extract year from enrollment date
questions.description: Return first_name and the year they enrolled.
hints: strftime('%Y', date) extracts the year as a string
CAST to INTEGER for numeric comparison
questions.explanation: strftime formats dates; %Y returns the 4-digit year.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, CAST(strftime('%Y', enrollment_date) AS INTEGER) AS enrollment_year FROM students

questions.title: Students enrolled in even-numbered years
questions.description: Return first_name, enrollment_date for students enrolled in even-numbered years.
hints: Extract year with strftime('%Y', ...)
Cast to INTEGER
Modulo 2 checks evenness
questions.explanation: strftime + modulo enables filtering by numeric properties of dates.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, enrollment_date FROM students WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y', enrollment_date) AS INTEGER) % 2 = 0

questions.title: Months since enrollment
questions.description: Return first_name and the number of months since each student enrolled (as of 2024-06-01).
hints: julianday difference divided by ~30.44 gives approximate months
CAST to INTEGER truncates decimals
This is an approximation
questions.explanation: Approximate month calculation uses average days per month.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, CAST((julianday('2024-06-01') - julianday(enrollment_date)) / 30.44 AS INTEGER) AS months_enrolled FROM students

questions.title: Students with no advisor
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name for students whose advisor_teacher_id is NULL.
hints: Use IS NULL for null column check
advisor_teacher_id can be NULL for some students
questions.explanation: IS NULL is the only correct way to test for null values.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE advisor_teacher_id IS NULL

questions.title: Replace NULL advisors with Unassigned
questions.description: Return first_name and advisor_teacher_id, replacing NULL with Unassigned.
hints: COALESCE returns first non-null value
CAST integer to TEXT so COALESCE works
Replace NULL with literal string
questions.explanation: COALESCE(val, fallback) is like IFNULL but accepts multiple args.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, COALESCE(CAST(advisor_teacher_id AS TEXT), 'Unassigned') AS advisor FROM students

questions.title: Count enrollments with vs without grades
questions.description: Return count of enrollments that have a grade and count that don't.
hints: CASE WHEN...END acts as conditional counting
IS NOT NULL vs IS NULL branches
Sum each branch separately
questions.explanation: Conditional aggregation uses CASE inside aggregate functions.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN grade IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS graded, SUM(CASE WHEN grade IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ungraded FROM enrollments

questions.title: Students with incomplete addresses
questions.description: Return first_name, address, city, state for students where ANY address field is NULL.
hints: Check each address component with OR
If any is NULL, include the row
Multiple OR conditions
questions.explanation: OR chains catch any null across multiple columns.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, address, city, state FROM students WHERE address IS NULL OR city IS NULL OR state IS NULL OR zip_code IS NULL

questions.title: Active loans with no return date
questions.description: Return student_id, book_id, loan_date for active loans without a return_date.
hints: status = Active implies not yet returned
return_date IS NULL confirms no return recorded
questions.explanation: Active loans without a return_date represent ongoing borrows.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT student_id, book_id, loan_date FROM loans WHERE status = 'Active' AND return_date IS NULL

questions.title: Exam results with NULL marks
questions.description: Return exam title and course_number for exams where at least one result has NULL marks_obtained.
hints: Subquery finds exam_ids with NULL marks
Outer query gets exam details
JOIN through exams to courses
questions.explanation: NULL marks_obtained may indicate a student skipped the exam.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT e.title, c.course_number FROM exams e JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id WHERE e.id IN (SELECT exam_id FROM exam_results WHERE marks_obtained IS NULL)

questions.title: Rank students by GPA within each department
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name, department_id, gpa, and rank within each department by GPA descending.
hints: RANK() assigns rank within partition
PARTITION BY department_id
ORDER BY gpa DESC inside the window
questions.explanation: Window functions compute ranks/rolling stats without collapsing rows.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, department_id, gpa, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY gpa DESC) AS gpa_rank FROM students

questions.title: Running total of scholarship amounts
questions.description: Return student_id, scholarship_id, amount_awarded, and running total per student ordered by amount.
hints: PARTITION BY student_id creates per-student windows
ORDER BY amount_awarded for running sum
SUM as a window function computes cumulative total
questions.explanation: OVER() clause turns an aggregate into a window function.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT student_id, scholarship_id, amount_awarded, SUM(amount_awarded) OVER (PARTITION BY student_id ORDER BY amount_awarded) AS running_total FROM student_scholarships

questions.title: Row number of enrollments per course
questions.description: Assign a row number to each enrollment within a course, ordered by grade_points descending.
hints: PARTITION BY course_id groups rankings per course
ORDER BY grade_points DESC puts best grades first
NULLS LAST pushes missing grades to bottom
questions.explanation: ROW_NUMBER() gives unique sequential numbering within each partition.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT course_id, student_id, grade, grade_points, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY grade_points DESC NULLS LAST) AS enrollment_rank FROM enrollments WHERE status = 'Completed'

questions.title: Average GPA deviation per student
questions.description: Return first_name, gpa, and how much their GPA deviates from their department's average GPA.
hints: AVG() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) computes dept average
Subtract dept average from individual GPA
ROUND to 2 decimals for clean output
questions.explanation: Deviations measure how far each value is from its group mean.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, gpa, ROUND(gpa - AVG(gpa) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id), 2) AS gpa_deviation FROM students

questions.title: Lagged enrollment dates per student
questions.description: Return student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, and the previous enrollment_date for that student.
hints: LAG(col, 1) looks at the previous row
PARTITION BY student_id resets per student
ORDER BY enrollment_date for chronological lag
questions.explanation: LAG accesses prior-row values without self-joining.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, LAG(enrollment_date, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY student_id ORDER BY enrollment_date) AS prev_enrollment FROM enrollments

questions.title: Percentile rank of exam scores
questions.description: Return course_number, student first_name, last_name, marks_obtained, and percentile rank within the course.
hints: RANK() within course partition for position
COUNT(*) OVER gives total for that course
Formula converts rank to 0-100 percentile
questions.explanation: Percentile rank normalizes scores across different exams.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT c.course_number, s.first_name, s.last_name, er.marks_obtained, ROUND(100.0 * (RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.course_id ORDER BY er.marks_obtained) - 1) / (COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY e.course_id) - 1), 1) AS percentile_rank FROM exam_results er JOIN exams e ON er.exam_id = e.id JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id JOIN students s ON er.student_id = s.id

questions.title: High-GPA students via CTE
questions.description: Using a CTE, return first_name, last_name, gpa for students with GPA >= 3.5.
hints: Define CTE named high_gpa
Filter gpa >= 3.5 inside CTE
SELECT from the CTE afterwards
questions.explanation: CTEs improve readability by naming intermediate result sets.
questions.solutionSql: WITH high_gpa AS (SELECT first_name, last_name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa >= 3.5) SELECT * FROM high_gpa

questions.title: Department GPA summary via CTE
questions.description: Using a CTE, return department name and average GPA.
hints: Define CTE dept_avg with grouped GPAs
JOIN CTE result to departments for names
Clean readable structure
questions.explanation: CTEs make complex multi-step queries easier to read and maintain.
questions.solutionSql: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT department_id, ROUND(AVG(gpa), 2) AS avg_gpa FROM students GROUP BY department_id) SELECT d.name, da.avg_gpa FROM dept_avg da JOIN departments d ON da.department_id = d.id

questions.title: Top student per department via CTE
questions.description: Using a CTE with RANK(), return the top-GPA student in each department.
hints: CTE ranks students within each department
Filter rnk = 1 to keep only top student per dept
WINDOW function inside CTE
questions.explanation: Combining CTEs with window functions is a powerful pattern.
questions.solutionSql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT first_name, last_name, department_id, gpa, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY gpa DESC) AS rnk FROM students) SELECT first_name, last_name, department_id, gpa FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1

questions.title: Cumulative enrollment counts via CTE
questions.description: Using a CTE, show semester and total enrollments per semester for Fall 2023 and Spring 2024.
hints: Group enrollments by semester and year
Count statuses that indicate activity
Format period as semester + year
questions.explanation: CTEs can pre-aggregate data before final formatting.
questions.solutionSql: WITH sem_counts AS (SELECT semester, year, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM enrollments WHERE status IN ('Completed', 'In Progress') GROUP BY semester, year) SELECT semester || ' ' || CAST(year AS TEXT) AS period, cnt FROM sem_counts ORDER BY year, semester

questions.title: Overdue loan report via CTE
questions.description: Using a CTE, list active loans where due_date is before 2024-02-01, with student name and book title.
hints: CTE identifies overdue active loans
JOIN to students and books for names
Combine CTE with standard joins
questions.explanation: CTEs help separate identification logic from display logic.
questions.solutionSql: WITH overdue AS (SELECT student_id, book_id, due_date FROM loans WHERE status = 'Active' AND due_date < '2024-02-01') SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, b.title, o.due_date FROM overdue o JOIN students s ON o.student_id = s.id JOIN books b ON o.book_id = b.id

questions.title: Department workload report via CTE
questions.description: Using a CTE, show each department's teacher count and the total subjects they teach.
hints: Two CTEs: one for teacher counts, one for subject counts
LEFT JOIN both to departments to keep all depts
COALESCE handles departments with zero teachers or subjects
questions.explanation: Multiple CTEs can pre-compute independent aggregates.
questions.solutionSql: WITH teacher_counts AS (SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS tc FROM teachers GROUP BY department_id), subject_counts AS (SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS sc FROM subjects GROUP BY department_id) SELECT d.name, COALESCE(tc.tc, 0) AS teachers, COALESCE(sc.sc, 0) AS subjects FROM departments d LEFT JOIN teacher_counts tc ON d.id = tc.department_id LEFT JOIN subject_counts sc ON d.id = sc.department_id

questions.title: Insert a new student
questions.description: Fix the INSERT statement to add a student with id=31, first_name='Nina', last_name='Patel', email='nina.patel@logixzen.edu', date_of_birth='2003-04-10', gender='Female', status='Active', gpa=3.60, department_id=2, advisor_teacher_id=5.
hints: Make sure all required columns are listed
Values must match column order exactly
Use single quotes for strings, no quotes for numbers
questions.explanation: INSERT adds a new row to the table.
questions.solutionSql: INSERT INTO students (id, first_name, last_name, email, date_of_birth, gender, status, gpa, department_id, advisor_teacher_id) VALUES (31, 'Nina', 'Patel', 'nina.patel@logixzen.edu', '2003-04-10', 'Female', 'Active', 3.60, 2, 5)

questions.title: Update a student GPA
questions.description: Fix the UPDATE statement to change student id=5's GPA to 3.90.
hints: SET specifies the column and new value
WHERE targets the specific student
Always verify the WHERE clause before executing updates
questions.explanation: UPDATE modifies existing rows based on conditions.
questions.solutionSql: UPDATE students SET gpa = 3.90 WHERE id = 5

questions.title: Delete dropped enrollments
questions.description: Fix the DELETE statement to remove all enrollments with status 'Dropped'.
hints: DELETE syntax: DELETE FROM table WHERE condition
Only dropped enrollments should be removed
Double-check WHERE before running DELETE — it is irreversible in SQL
questions.explanation: DELETE removes rows matching the condition permanently.
questions.solutionSql: DELETE FROM enrollments WHERE status = 'Dropped'

questions.title: Insert a new book with author
questions.description: Insert a new book (id=21, isbn='978-0-00-000000-0', title='1984 Special Edition', price=14.99, stock=10, category='Fiction', subject_id=9) and add its author (author_id=2, book_id=21).
hints: Two INSERT statements needed
First insert the book, then add the author link
Maintain referential integrity — book must exist before adding to book_authors
questions.explanation: Related inserts require ordering to respect foreign keys.
questions.brokenQuery: INSERT INTO books VALUES (21, '978-0-00-000000-0', '1984 Special Edition', 14.99, 10, 'Fiction', 9);
questions.solutionSql:
INSERT INTO books (id, isbn, title, price, stock, category, subject_id) VALUES (21, '978-0-00-000000-0', '1984 Special Edition', 14.99, 10, 'Fiction', 9)
INSERT INTO book_authors (book_id, author_id) VALUES (21, 2)

questions.title: Update book prices with discount
questions.description: Fix the UPDATE statement to reduce all Fiction book prices by 10 percent.
hints: Use ROUND to keep prices to 2 decimal places
Multiply by 0.9 for a 10 percent reduction
WHERE limits the update to Fiction category books only
questions.explanation: Updates can use expressions to compute new values.
questions.solutionSql: UPDATE books SET price = ROUND(price * 0.9, 2) WHERE category = 'Fiction'

questions.title: Archive completed exams
questions.description: Fix the UPDATE to mark all enrollments for Fall 2023 courses as Completed if they are In Progress.
hints: Subquery finds Fall 2023 course IDs
Outer UPDATE changes In Progress to Completed for those courses
Nested subqueries in UPDATE are supported by SQLite
questions.explanation: Updates with subqueries allow conditional updates based on other tables.
questions.solutionSql: UPDATE enrollments SET status = 'Completed' WHERE status = 'In Progress' AND course_id IN (SELECT id FROM courses WHERE semester = 'Fall' AND year = 2023)

questions.title: Create a grading logs table
questions.description: Write CREATE TABLE to store exam grading logs with columns: id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY), exam_id (INTEGER NOT NULL), grader_notes (TEXT), created_at (TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP).
hints: Each column needs a name, type, and optional constraints
DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP auto-fills created_at
PRIMARY KEY makes id the unique identifier
questions.explanation: CREATE TABLE defines a new schema object.
questions.solutionSql: CREATE TABLE grading_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, exam_id INTEGER NOT NULL, grader_notes TEXT, created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)

questions.title: Add a column to students
questions.description: Write ALTER TABLE to add a phone_alternate column (TEXT) to the students table.
hints: ALTER TABLE adds a column
ADD COLUMN is the syntax
New column defaults to NULL for existing rows
questions.explanation: ALTER TABLE modifies an existing table's structure.
questions.brokenQuery: ALTER TABLE students ADD phone_alternate TEXT
questions.solutionSql: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN phone_alternate TEXT

questions.title: Create a view for student transcripts
questions.description: Write CREATE VIEW to show student transcript data: student id, full name, course_number, grade, and enrollment_date.
hints: Views are virtual tables based on a query
JOIN three tables for the transcript view
Column aliases make the output clearer
questions.explanation: CREATE VIEW stores a query definition for repeated use.
questions.brokenQuery: CREATE VIEW v_student_transcript AS SELECT * FROM students JOIN enrollments
questions.solutionSql: CREATE VIEW v_student_transcript AS SELECT s.id AS student_id, s.first_name || ' ' || s.last_name AS full_name, c.course_number, e.grade, e.enrollment_date FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id

questions.title: Create index for faster lookups
questions.description: Write CREATE INDEX on students(department_id) to speed up department-based queries.
hints: INDEX names typically start with idx_
Specify the table and column(s) to index
Indexes speed up WHERE and JOIN operations on the indexed column
questions.explanation: CREATE INDEX improves query performance on frequently filtered columns.
questions.solutionSql: CREATE INDEX idx_students_department ON students(department_id)

questions.title: Find departments with head teachers
questions.description: Return department name and head teacher name where head_teacher_id is not NULL.
hints: JOIN departments to teachers on head_teacher_id
Filter where head_teacher_id IS NOT NULL
Concatenate teacher name for display
questions.explanation: Foreign key constraints ensure head_teacher_id references a valid teacher.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT d.name, t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS head_name FROM departments d JOIN teachers t ON d.head_teacher_id = t.id WHERE d.head_teacher_id IS NOT NULL

questions.title: Verify unique constraint on email
questions.description: Show all students whose email domain is duplicated (more than one student shares the same @domain).
hints: Extract domain from email using SUBSTR and INSTR
GROUP BY domain
HAVING COUNT > 1 finds duplicates
questions.explanation: Email has a UNIQUE constraint so duplicates should not occur in valid data.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1) AS domain, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM students GROUP BY SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1) HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

questions.title: Check referential integrity enrollments courses
questions.description: Find any enrollment referencing a non-existent course_id (orphaned records).
hints: LEFT JOIN enrollments to courses
WHERE c.id IS NULL finds orphans
Should return zero rows if data is consistent
questions.explanation: Referential integrity checks detect data quality issues.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT e.id FROM enrollments e LEFT JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id WHERE c.id IS NULL

questions.title: Validate loan foreign keys
questions.description: Find any loan referencing a student or book that no longer exists.
hints: LEFT JOIN loans to both students and books
Check either side for NULL
Both FKs must reference existing records
questions.explanation: Validating all foreign keys ensures the database remains consistent.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT l.id, l.student_id, l.book_id FROM loans l LEFT JOIN students s ON l.student_id = s.id LEFT JOIN books b ON l.book_id = b.id WHERE s.id IS NULL OR b.id IS NULL

questions.title: Simulate transaction-safe enrollment
questions.description: Show the course_id and available spots for course_id = 1.
hints: Subtract enrolled_count from max_students to get available spots
WHERE enrolled_count < max_students filters full courses
This simulates a capacity check before enrollment
questions.explanation: Transaction safety checks happen before mutation operations.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT id AS course_id, max_students - enrolled_count AS available_spots FROM courses WHERE id = 1 AND enrolled_count < max_students

questions.title: Check department budget before hiring
questions.description: Show departments with enough budget (> 80000) to hire a new teacher at average salary.
hints: Filter departments with budget exceeding 80000
Subtract estimated salary to show surplus
Only budget-surplus departments can afford a new hire
questions.explanation: Budget checks are part of transactional decision-making.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT name, budget, budget - 80000 AS surplus FROM departments WHERE budget > 80000

questions.title: Validate school year transition
questions.description: Find courses from Fall 2023 that have corresponding Spring 2024 offerings (course_number match).
hints: Self-join courses on course_number
Match Fall 2023 with Spring 2024
Returns courses continuing to the next semester
questions.explanation: Self-joins validate continuity across time periods.
questions.solutionSql: SELECT fall.course_number, fall.year AS fall_year, spring.year AS spring_year FROM courses fall JOIN courses spring ON fall.course_number = spring.course_number WHERE fall.semester = 'Fall' AND fall.year = 2023 AND spring.semester = 'Spring' AND spring.year = 2024

questions.title: Calculate net scholarship disbursement
questions.description: Show total scholarships awarded per department (via student department mapping).
hints: JOIN student_scholarships to students to departments
SUM(amount_awarded) per department
ORDER BY total descending
questions.explanation: Aggregated financial reports require multi-table joins.

questions.title: Pivot enrollment status counts

questions.title: Calculate class rank within department

questions.title: Find students with above-average exam grades
questions.description: Return first_name, last_name of students whose average exam marks exceed the overall average exam mark.

questions.title: List all subjects with enrollment statistics
questions.description: Return subject name, total courses, and total enrollments.
hints: LEFT JOIN preserves subjects with zero courses

questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN ensures no subject is lost even with zero enrollments.

questions.title: Detect grade inflation midterm vs final
questions.description: Return course_number, midterm_avg, final_avg for courses where final average exceeds midterm average.
hints: Conditional aggregation separates Midterm and Final averages

ROUND for readable output
questions.explanation: CASE inside AVG enables side-by-side metric comparison.

questions.title: Build a student transcript query
questions.description: Return full transcript: student name, course_number, section, semester, year, grade for all completed enrollments.

Filter to Completed enrollments only
Order by student name, then year, then semester
questions.explanation: Transcripts are classic real-world reporting queries.

questions.title: Library checkout report
questions.description: Show which students currently have books checked out (active loans), including book title and due date.
hints: Status = Active means not yet returned
Join three tables for full context
Show due_date so librarian can track overdue items
questions.explanation: Active loan reports help librarians manage circulation.

questions.title: Dean's list candidates
questions.description: Identify students eligible for Dean's List: GPA >= 3.5, status = Active, and at least one Completed enrollment.

Must have at least one Completed enrollment

questions.title: Department spending report
questions.description: Return department name, total teacher salary, and total department budget with surplus/deficit.

COALESCE handles NULL salary sums
Surplus/deficit = budget minus total salaries
questions.explanation: Financial reports require careful NULL handling.

questions.title: Course enrollment heat map
questions.description: For each course, show course_number, section, semester, year, and how full it is (enrolled vs max).

questions.title: Examination schedule report

questions.title: Book borrowing trends by student
questions.description: Show each student's first_name, last_name, total books borrowed, and total fines paid.

COUNT(loans) and SUM(fine) per student
